146449072.title: File:103. Горење железна волна во кислород.webm

Categories.value: Oxygen|Combustion|Steel wool|Chemistry Wikiexperiments

ImageDescription.value:
Red-hot iron wool placed in a tube filled with O<sub>2</sub> ignites and burns with intense light. When iron is burned, metal oxides are formed. Depending on the reaction conditions and the ratio between the two participants, the following equations can be written:
<dl><dd>2Fe + O<sub>2</sub> = 2FeO</dd>
<dd>4Fe + 3O<sub>2</sub> = 2Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub></dd>
<dd>3Fe + 2O<sub>2</sub> = Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub></dd></dl>
The experiment was performed by Prof. PhD Miha Bukleski. The planning of the experiment also included the Prof. Emeritus PhD Vladimir Petruševski, Prof. PhD Marina Stojanovska and the student Mihail Trajkov, Department of Chemistry, FNSM, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje, Macedonia.
